name: Collapse disclosures expose aria-expanded and respond to the keyboard
description:
The run accordion and every FindingCard are built on the shared `Collapse` primitive: each trigger carries `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls`, and the body stays mounted for the ~180ms ddCollapseOut animation before it unmounts. Counting `[aria-expanded]` is therefore both an a11y assertion and a mount assertion — a trigger that never wires the attribute, and a body that never unmounts, both fail here.

Targets PR #479: one agent run, one review accordion, four findings, so the counts are exact — 1 accordion trigger + 4 FindingCard triggers = 5. Two are open on arrival (the accordion via defaultOpen, plus the first finding card).

Every `wait 600` below outlasts ddCollapseOut on purpose; a shorter wait would read the body while it is still mounted and mis-assert.

`scrollintoview` before each click is mandatory, not tidiness: agent-browser's `find ... click` silently no-ops on a below-the-fold element, exiting 0 with '✓ Done' while the click never lands.

Read-only seeded data (no model call).

land on the PR list

steps.label: open PR #479 by title, not by row position
navigate to the PR detail route
PR detail data settles
switch to the Agent runs tab
findings tab is active in the URL
every disclosure trigger is wired: 1 run accordion + 4 FindingCards
two arrive open — the run accordion and the first finding card
all four finding cards are mounted inside the open accordion
bring the run accordion trigger into the viewport before clicking it
collapse the run accordion
outlast the ~180ms ddCollapseOut animation so the body has really unmounted
collapsing unmounts the body: only the accordion trigger itself is left
and that surviving trigger reports itself collapsed
no finding card outlives the collapse
re-expand the run accordion
let the open animation settle
the body comes back with all four card triggers
and restores the same two open disclosures
keyboard-focus the first COLLAPSED finding-card trigger
activate it with Enter — these triggers are div[role=button], so Enter must be handled by hand
let the open animation settle
Enter opened a third disclosure — the card body is keyboard-reachable
